target.statement: At one fixed base point r* and for every finite two-channel agent network satisfying the frozen typed hypotheses, establish the exact pointwise meta-agent RG package: channelwise zero weighted edge distortion is equivalent to a unique holonomy-stabilized common root marginal; the unrestricted forward-KL barycenter is the unique mixture with the stated holonomy qualifications; small edge distortion yields the stated total-variation diameter bounds; normalized scalar attention coarsens exactly by pushing joint endpoint-event laws and disintegrating, while the additional incidence-supported component-rooted tier retains component-indexed conditional laws of dressed boundary marks and internal based holonomy; a recognition-independent common coarse Markov channel obeys the exact VFE conditional-KL defect; nested memberships and a declared moving inference flow obey their typed composition and semiconjugacy laws; and the eight named shortcut claims are refuted by contained counterexamples. The result constructs only paired marginal parents and asserts no extension across R.
target.quantifiers: For every fixed base point r*; every finite nonempty vertex set; each of the separately typed belief and model support graphs satisfying the frozen connected reciprocal-groupoid hypotheses; every family of normalized vertex laws, positive normalized vertex and barycenter weights, conditional attention rows, and bimeasurable invertible edge transports; every comparison law for which the displayed extended KL quantities are defined; and every declared normalized membership or common coarse channel satisfying the stated side conditions, the exact identities, equivalences, bounds, and composition laws in the target hold. For the retained-mark conjunct, endpoint assignments are supported on declared membership incidences and every parent-incidence support is refined channelwise into connected components with one rooted spanning tree per component. For the explicitly named invalid shortcuts, there exists the contained finite or Gaussian counterexample. Compact and noncompact holonomy and dynamic conclusions are restricted exactly as stated.
domains: One fixed overlap point r*; no neighborhood, section, or extension across the contextual base R is in the target.

A finite nonempty vertex set V and, for each channel x in {q,m}, a connected underlying positive-support graph with a reciprocal path groupoid generated by bimeasurable bijections Omega^x_ij: Z^x_j -> Z^x_i and Omega^x_ji=(Omega^x_ij)^(-1).
Standard-Borel sample fibers Z^q_i and Z^m_i with normalized laws q_i(r*) and m_i(r*); legacy notation s_i may denote m_i but does not change its type.

Separate conditional rows beta_ij and gamma_ij, positive normalized receiver weights alpha^q_i and alpha^m_i, joint edge-event laws eta^q_ij=alpha^q_i beta_ij and eta^m_ij=alpha^m_i gamma_ij, and positive normalized barycenter weights w^q_i and w^m_i.

Normalized hard or soft membership kernels C(A|i), explicitly declared normalized correlated endpoint kernels K(A,B|i,j) where used, and standard-Borel recognition-independent common coarse Markov channels for VFE comparison. For retained marks, K is supported on C(A|i)>0 and C(B|j)>0, and each support V_A={i:C(A|i)>0} is refined channelwise into connected components of the induced positive-support transport graph with one rooted spanning tree per component.
Optional finite-dimensional smooth fine and coarse state manifolds, a C1 moving coarse map C_t, and declared fine/coarse inference vector fields for the dynamic semiconjugacy statement.
codomains: Holonomy-fixed normalized root-law fibers and their paired belief/model marginal parents.

Extended nonnegative KL distortions, total-variation bounds, normalized coarse joint edge-event laws and conditional rows, component-indexed conditional mark kernels whose component sums recover scalar parent-pair event masses, and exact conditional-KL VFE residuals.
Typed nested coarse channels and, only after a flow is declared, coarse inference trajectories satisfying the moving-map semiconjugacy equation.
target.regularity: All graph sums are finite. Probability laws are normalized on standard-Borel spaces. Edge transports are bimeasurable bijections, so pushforward preserves equality, total variation, and relative entropy with the extended support convention. Regular conditional laws are used only on standard-Borel spaces and only up to the stated almost-sure equivalence. The unrestricted mixture theorem uses Radon-Nikodym derivatives and extended values. Compact-Haar claims additionally require a measurable action, a common dominating measure, and the stated finite-KL/integrability hypotheses. The moving-map formula requires C1 time and state dependence along a declared differentiable flow.
measures: Normalized vertex belief and model probability laws on their declared standard-Borel fibers.
Finite normalized receiver, source, endpoint-membership, and joint edge-event laws.
Normalized counting measure on finite holonomy groups and normalized Haar probability on compact holonomy closures when the compact theorem is invoked.
The common evidence and posterior/recognition laws used in the exact VFE chain rule.
boundary_conditions: KL is extended valued: failure of absolute continuity gives +infinity; no infinity-minus-infinity expression is used.
Rows with zero pushed receiver mass are immaterial conditional versions; null edge events carry no conditional mark law.
Approximate total-variation bounds require finite total edge distortion, a strictly positive minimum over the finite positive edge weights used by the path bound, and finite graph diameter.
Literal replicated covers are not normalized membership kernels and retain their multiplicity instead of being silently mass normalized.

Scalar event-law pushforward is valid for every normalized endpoint kernel; retained marks additionally require membership-incidence support and component rooting, and no single root is assigned to a disconnected parent support.
The constant-metric Gaussian stability corollary excludes adaptive rows, nonlinear full-law VFE dynamics, moving memberships, and rank-changing metric strata.
Hyperedge or shared-factor closure and full path-law or memory-kernel closure require separate joint-factor, path-law, or linear-dynamic hypotheses and are outside this target.
symmetries: Passive vertex-frame rechoices conjugate based holonomy and transform boundary marks by their two endpoint frames while leaving scalar event masses invariant.

Changing a component root or its spanning tree changes only that component-rooted presentation; transported laws and marks are compared through the induced bimeasurable conjugacy within the component.
Typed vertex and parent relabelings act by pushforward and do not identify belief and model channels.
target.equivalence: Probability laws are equal as normalized measures; conditional kernels are equal almost surely under their conditioning law; component-rooted presentations are equivalent only by one simultaneous root-frame transformation in each component, with the relative orientation of root features, holonomy, and boundary marks retained. Belief and model parents remain a typed pair and are not identified with a joint law.
premises: The repository convention is Omega_ij: j -> i, and path products are ordered accordingly.
Each positive-support channel graph is connected for the one-root statements; disconnected graphs receive the same theorem componentwise and are outside the one-root wording.
All receiver and barycenter weights declared positive are strictly positive and normalized; beta and gamma are normalized conditional rows on their declared supports.

For marked closure, endpoint assignments are supported on declared membership incidences, and each channel-specific induced parent support is decomposed into connected components and rooted separately.
Full-frame connection-Laplacian claims use the existing finite fixed-K represented sector, reciprocal invertible links, and positive-definite internal edge weights.

The VFE comparison uses one declared recognition-independent normalized channel applied to both the posterior and recognition law without changing the observation coordinate or evidence representative.
No premise supplies a joint belief-model law, a canonical partition, an autonomous agent, an extension across R, physical time, a continuum limit, or an intrinsic threshold.
permitted_theorems: Radon-Nikodym chain rules, KL nonnegativity and zero criterion, finite-mixture domination, and the standard-Borel relative-entropy disintegration theorem with hypotheses mapped in the contained derivation.
Pinsker's inequality and the total-variation triangle inequality; no KL triangle inequality is permitted.
Finite graph spanning-tree and fundamental-cycle generation of the reciprocal path groupoid.
Normalized finite-kernel pushforward, disintegration, and tower-property composition.

The repository's proved kernel-holonomy fixed-space isomorphism, full-Gaussian forward-KL barycenter, compact-Haar Gaussian specialization, component-indexed marked-event pushforward, and exact coarse-VFE chain rule, each used only at its stated scope.
The ordinary chain rule for a C1 time-dependent map evaluated along a declared differentiable flow.
target.falsification_criterion: A counterexample within the frozen typed hypotheses to any conjunct of the target, a support case in which a displayed extended identity is undefined or false, a failure of uniqueness, or a dependency whose contained derivation does not prove its exact ledger statement refutes the affirmative conjunction. Failure of an explicitly excluded continuum, partition-selection, ontology, or physical-time extension does not refute the pointwise target.
